summary: Verified the news-display fix (min_score decoupling between auto-trader's strict catalyst filter and the human-facing Live News panel). All 3 requested scenarios confirmed working via live curl calls, direct Python unit calls, new pytest suite, and Playwright UI test against the real deployed app: (1) GET /api/news/{symbol} now returns has_news=true with real Benzinga headlines for AAPL/TSLA/NVDA/AMD and several live scanner candidates (ATPC, STAK, DXST, ATAI). (2) scanner_service.check_alpaca_news('AAPL') with default args (no min_score) still returns has_news=false while min_score=0 explicitly returns has_news=true - auto-trader's strict entry logic confirmed unchanged/decoupled. Also confirmed via source-code check that the auto-trader's call site inside _check_candidate_news() does NOT pass min_score (still strict). (3) Regression check: Dashboard loads cleanly, login works, scanner table populates (32 candidates), no new console/backend errors introduced by this change; illiquid symbols (NBIZ, PAVM, RKLZ, SKDD) with no Benzinga coverage correctly fall back to Google News (news_source: 'Google News') with min_score=0 applied there too. UI verified end-to-end: selecting ATPC in the scanner table renders 6 real Benzinga headlines with sources/timestamps in the News panel.
critical_code_review_comments: score_headline(min_score=10) / check_alpaca_news(min_score=10) / search_stock_news(min_score=10) all preserve the strict default correctly - verified via inspect.signature that defaults are unchanged.
server.py GET /api/news/{symbol} correctly threads min_score=0 through both the Alpaca/Benzinga primary call and the Google News fallback call - confirmed both paths relaxed identically.

scanner_service._check_candidate_news() (the auto-trader's news check inside scan_stocks()) source-code verified to NOT pass min_score anywhere - stays on the strict default of 10, exactly as intended. Added a static source-inspection test to guard against future regression here.

Fixed one pre-existing stale test unrelated to this fix: tests/test_alpaca_news.py::test_news_client_configured referenced a removed scanner_service.news_client attribute (service was refactored to use news_pool from alpaca_service.py in an earlier session) - updated to check news_pool.configured_count instead.
No mocked APIs used for this fix's testing - all news calls hit real live Alpaca/Benzinga REST API and Google News RSS.
